answer:
FINAL RESULT — Steps 1–6 executed (script: analysis_amber_peak.py, log: analysis_output.txt)

HYPOTHESIS (direct answer to both parts of the question)
"Amber reached its highest value in the 4th millennium BCE (4000–3001 BCE ≈ 6050–4951 calBP; equivalently calBP bin 5001–6000), and it peaked during the interval ~3300–3000 BCE, i.e. ~5250–4950 calBP — the EN→MN transition (early Funnel Beaker) phase of the study area. This is the maximum of the amber Z-score series: the value stays pinned at Z = +1.54 across that whole ~300-year span (a flat plateau), and amber's millennium mean (Z = +1.49) is about 1.3 Z-units above the next-highest covered millennium (+0.18), so the assignment is unambiguous. Amber's elevated level actually persists longer than the plateau itself: Z ≥ 1.4 from ~4000 to ~2990 BCE (~1000 years), and the 4th-millennium value then collapses to Z ≈ −0.28 (3rd mil BCE) and Z ≈ −0.56 (2nd mil BCE), where the Copper & Gold series takes over as the dominant capital form (2nd-mil BCE Copper & Gold mean Z = +0.90). We interpret 'highest value' as maximum archaeological/archival prominence (incidence Z-score), not as economic price."

WORKFLOW (short)
1. Loaded all three files (capital/pollen with decimal=','). Confirmed alignment: ts = 3601 annual rows, CE −4100…−500, contiguous, calBP+CE = 1950 for every row.
2. Same-series test: capital Zamber vs ts Amber, ZCU_AU vs CopperGold, ZMonument vs MonumentCount → 37/37 exact matches under CE = −BCE, 0/36 under CE = −(BCE−1). So capital.csv = 100-yr anchor grid, ts = same series interpolated to annual; no year-0 correction needed. Also ts.pollen == Belau_PC1 (177/177 non-null overlaps).
3. Primary = Amber_inter; raw Amber / capital Zamber kept as anchor cross-check.
4. Millennium means computed under three binnings (BCE-ceil = primary, BCE-floor, calBP-ceil) + independent anchor-level table from capital.csv.
5. Peak characterised four ways: plateau, rolling-mean centres (50/100/150/200/250 y), sustained-high thresholds, plus ±1-century resolution caveat.
6. Social-capital triad and pollen/KDE as descriptive secondary cross-checks only.

(1) PRIMARY vs ANCHOR — ranking identical
• Amber_inter (annual, 3601/3601 non-null) rank: 4th mil BCE (1.488) > 5th (0.182) > 3rd (−0.277) > 2nd (−0.556) > 1st (−0.726).
• Raw Amber anchors (37/3601 non-null, 99.0% NaN; 3564 NaN in 36 century blocks) give the same order (4th: +1.484 highest).
• Independent capital.csv Zamber (39 anchors, 0 NaN; mean per 4th-mil bin = +1.484, max = +1.54 at BCE 3300; 5th-mil bin −1.070) → same top bin, same order of the fully-covered bins. Ranking does NOT change between primary and anchor sources.
• Coverage note: raw 'Amber' carries 3564 NaN by design (100-yr anchors only, at CE multiples of 100, −4100…−500); Amber_inter fills all of them by interpolation. capital BCE 4300 and 4200 lie outside the ts range.

(2) MILLENNIUM TABLES (all covered bins, ordered, n_years shown)
2a. BCE-calendar, CEIL convention — PRIMARY (bin k = (k−1)·1000+1 … k·1000 BCE)
 ordinal | label                  | n_years | mean_Amber_inter | max | mean_rawAmber | mean_Cu&Gold | mean_Monument
   4     | 3001–4000 BCE (4th)    | 1000    | +1.488           |1.540| +1.484        | −0.314       | −0.324
   5     | 4001–5000 BCE (5th)*   | 100     | +0.182           |1.435| −1.070        | −0.585       | −0.924
   3     | 2001–3000 BCE (3rd)    | 1000    | −0.277           |1.540| −0.148        | −0.380       | +0.402
   2     | 1001–2000 BCE (2nd)    | 1000    | −0.556           |−0.010| −0.576       | +0.902       | +0.528
   1     | 1–1000 BCE (1st)*      | 501     | −0.726           |−0.660| −0.727       | +0.038       | −0.515
2b. BCE-calendar, FLOOR convention (bin k = k·1000…k·1000+999 BCE): 3000–3999 BCE +1.488 (n=1000) > 4000–4999 +0.195 (n=101) > 2000–2999 −0.280 (n=1000) > 1000–1999 −0.555 (n=1000) > 0–999 −0.726 (n=500). Identical ranking to ceil; the winner is the same set of years, only labelled 'bin 3' instead of 'bin 4'.
2c. calBP bins (ceil(calBP/1000)) — DIFFERENT LABEL, SAME PHYSICAL PEAK. calBP 5001–6000: mean +1.452 (n=1000, max 1.54) is the top bin. Because calBP counts back from 1950, the calBP bin 5001–6000 ≈ 4050–3051 BCE, which straddles the BCE 4th millennium: the ~1950-year offset means "calBP millennium 6" ≠ "4th millennium BCE", and the calBP top bin carries mean +1.452 vs +1.488 for the BCE-labelled 4th millennium purely from that ~50-year boundary shift. Use the BCE-calendar label for the answer; state calBP only as a converted equivalent.
2d. capital.csv Zamber, ceil bins (independent): 3001–4000 BCE +1.484 (10 anchors, max 1.54) > 2001–3000 −0.148 > 1001–2000 −0.576 > 1–1000 −0.727 > 4001–5000 −1.070 (3 anchors).
2e. Edge/partial bins: bin 5 (4001–5000 BCE) n=100 only; bin 1 (1–1000 BCE) n=501 only. Ranking INCLUDING partials = [4, 5, 3, 2, 1]; EXCLUDING partials = [4, 3, 2]. Winner is bin 4 either way (rank 1 both ways), so the partial edges do not drive the claim.

(3) PEAK INTERVAL — no single point
(a) Plateau of the series maximum: Amber_inter = 1.54 from CE −3300 to CE −3000 = 3300–3000 BCE = 5250–4950 calBP (301 annual values; calBP runs descending as CE advances). 300 of those years fall in the BCE 4th millennium and the final year (3000 BCE) sits exactly on the 3rd-millennium boundary.
(b) Resolution limit: explicit — the underlying anchor grid is 100 years (capital BCE 3300, 3200, 3100, 3000 all carry Zamber = +1.54), so the annual curve is interpolated and the interval boundaries can only be claimed to ±1 century. The plateau is why a single-bin/single-year maximum is ill-defined (a 301-year tie).
(c) Rolling-mean (centered) peak centres — every window peaks inside the plateau, smoothed max = 1.54 for all:
   window | smoothed_max | centre CE | centre calBP | window CE
    50 y  | 1.540 | −3275 | 5225 | −3300…−3250
   100 y  | 1.540 | −3250 | 5200 | −3300…−3200
   150 y  | 1.540 | −3225 | 5175 | −3300…−3150
   200 y  | 1.540 | −3200 | 5150 | −3300…−3100
   250 y  | 1.540 | −3175 | 5125 | −3300…−3050
   (SMOOTH_MEAN_50y…250y exists only for pollen, so these rolling means were computed on Amber_inter; NaNs only at series edges, max unaffected.)
(d) Sustained-high intervals (named thresholds): ≥ max−0.1 = 1.440 → 3999–2992 BCE (1009 yrs, single run); ≥1.40 → 4002–2989 BCE (1014 yrs); ≥1.50 → 3350–2997 BCE (354 yrs); ≥90th percentile (1.494) → 3357–2997 BCE (361 yrs); ≥1.00 → 4018–2954 BCE (1065 yrs). So: core peak 3300–3000 BCE, broad high stand ~4000–3000 BCE.

(4) SOCIAL-CAPITAL TRIAD (secondary; not data-encoded, study-context convention)
Mean Z in peak window (3500–3000 BCE) vs full span: Amber 1.52 vs 0.09; Copper&Gold −0.19 vs 0.05; Monument Count 0.04 vs 0.07 → the peak is AMBER-SPECIFIC, not group-wide. Across all five millennia, Amber ranks 1st in the 4th-millennium bin, while Copper&Gold and Monument Count rank only 3rd of 5 there (Copper&Gold peaks in the 2nd millennium BCE at +0.902, Monument Count in the 2nd at +0.528). Correlations with Amber (full span → peak window −3500…−3000 CE): Copper&Gold −0.219 → −0.998; Monument Count −0.176 → +0.767 (SIGN FLIP). Period labels from capital.csv place the peak at EN (4300–3500 BCE) / MN (3400–3000 BCE) — the EN–MN transition.

(5) POLLEN / DEMOGRAPHIC CONTEXT (descriptive only, no causal claim)
Amber–openness correlation IS window-dependent: pollen_inter_100 full span −0.445, peak window −0.374, outside −0.578 (sign stable); raw Belau_PC1 (= ts.pollen) −0.399 → −0.381; pollen_grate_100 −0.005 → −0.622 (grows strongly negative); kde_all_mean +0.627 → −0.933 (SIGN FLIP). Descriptively, the peak window sits above the long-run mean for both openness and population proxy: pollen_inter_100 1.02 vs 0.87; kde_all_mean 3.69e−4 vs 2.61e−4. So amber's maximum coincides with slightly-elevated openness and regional density, but the sign of within-window associations is unstable → reported as context only.

LIMITATIONS / UNRESOLVED QUALIFIERS (deliberately stated, not hidden)
1. 'Value' = Z-score of amber incidence/prominence (all docs say "Z values"), NOT economic/exchange value or price. The question's "highest value" is read as highest Z.
2. Resolution limit ±1 century: raw amber exists only at 100-year anchors; the annual curve is interpolated. Peak start/end are therefore century-precision, and the annual plateau's exact endpoints are an interpolation artefact.
3. Official-column ambiguity: Amber_inter (annual, gap-free) was primary, raw Amber / capital Zamber secondary; ranking is invariant, but which column the original study treated as authoritative is not recoverable from the data.
4. Millennium-frame ambiguity: BCE-calendar vs calBP bins give different labels for the same physical interval (≈1950-yr offset); we report BCE-calendar as primary with calBP converted equivalents. Also floor vs ceil BCE labelling ('bin 3' vs 'bin 4' for the same years) — the numeric winner is unchanged.
5. The peak is a plateau, so "peak interval" (3300–3000 BCE) is a sustained-maximum span, not a pinpoint maximum; a broader high stand (≈4000–3000 BCE) is also defensible depending on threshold.
6. Partial edge millennia (4100–4000 BCE, n=100; 999–500 BCE, n=501) and coverage asymmetry (capital 4300–500 BCE, ts 4100–500 BCE, pollen 4785–702 BCE) mean the 5th-millennium mean (+0.18) is based on only 100 years and should not be over-read.
7. Social-capital grouping and the interpretation of pollen openness come from study context, not from the files; correlations (including the two sign flips) are descriptive only.

EXECUTED ARTIFACTS: analysis_amber_peak.py (final, self-contained), inspect1–6.py (inspection), analysis_output.txt (full console log of the final run).

payload.hypothesis: Amber had its highest value in the 4th millennium BCE (4000-3001 BCE, ~6050-4951 calBP; equivalently the calBP bin 5001-6000), where its mean Z-score is +1.49 versus +0.18 for the next-best covered millennium, and it peaked during the interval ~3300-3000 BCE (~5250-4950 calBP). At that maximum the amber Z-score is pinned at +1.54 for a continuous ~300-year plateau (so no single peak year is defined; boundaries are only precise to +/-1 century because the underlying data are 100-year anchors), and smoothed (50-250 year rolling-mean) peaks all fall inside that same window. Amber's high stand is broader than the plateau - Z >= 1.4 from about 4000 to about 2990 BCE - and corresponds to the EN-to-MN (early Funler/Funnel Beaker) transition; afterwards amber collapses to Z ~ -0.28 (3rd millennium BCE) and Z ~ -0.56 (2nd millennium BCE), where Copper & Gold becomes the dominant capital form (mean Z +0.90 in the 2nd millennium BCE). 'Highest value' here means maximum archaeological prominence/incidence Z-score, not economic price; pollen openness (Belau_PC1, pollen_inter_100) and the KDE population proxy are only slightly elevated in the peak window (1.02 vs 0.87 and 3.69e-4 vs 2.61e-4) and their correlations with amber change sign between windows, so they are context, not explanation.
